title: Finite truncation devissage for module-object complexes
statement: Let X be a scheme, R a commutative ring object in abelian sheaves on its pro-etale site, and P an isomorphism-closed triangulated object property in D(Mod_R). If P contains F[0] for every constructible R-module F, then P contains every bounded complex with constructible homology. Bounded constructibility is also invariant under isomorphisms.

proof.text: Transport homology along isomorphisms to get isomorphism invariance and apply the existing DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded theorem to the constructible module-object property. That generic theorem proves the following induction, without a new induction proof here. Induct on the length m of a cohomological interval [a,a+m-1]. At m=0 the object is zero by the t-structure. For the successor step let b=a+m and use the distinguished truncation triangle tau_<b K -> K -> tau_>=b K. Its third term is concentrated in degree b, hence is H^b(K)[-b], with constructible H^b(K). Its first term has one shorter interval and retains constructible homology: below b compare homology by the truncation triangle, and at or above b use its zero homology. Apply the induction hypothesis, shift stability, and distinguished-triangle closure. Finally choose an interval from boundedness.

proof_origin.note: Restored the reviewed B2 finite-truncation reduction; D3 repairs the consumer and uses C4’s landed tensor single-sheaf proof.

lean.statement:
lemma prop_of_boundedConstructibleModule {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {R : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}} [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R]
    (P : ObjectProperty
      (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R)))
    [P.IsTriangulated] [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
    (hP : ∀ F : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R,
      IsConstructibleModuleObject R F →
      P ((singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
    {K : _root_.DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R)}
    (hK : boundedConstructible R K) : P K
